WW Demo - Cooling Train Saturday Shutdown
WW Demo - Lift Station Seven-Day Response

safety_templates.name: Electrical Lockout/Tagout
safety_templates.instructions: Isolate electrical energy, apply lock/tag, and verify zero energy before work.

safety_templates.name: WW Demo - Process/Basin Isolation
safety_templates.instructions: Isolate the affected process train or basin, verify bypass capacity, and confirm a stable process condition before work.

safety_templates.name: WW Demo - Confined-Space Entry Permit
safety_templates.instructions: Confirm confined-space permit, atmospheric testing, attendant coverage, rescue plan, and continuous monitoring before entry.

safety_templates.name: WW Demo - UV Exposure Control
safety_templates.instructions: De-energize UV banks, verify shutters or covers, and confirm UV-rated eye and skin protection before opening modules.

safety_templates.name: WW Demo - Chemical/CIP Handling
safety_templates.instructions: Verify SDS controls, chemical-resistant PPE, eyewash availability, drain routing, and neutralization plan before chemical or CIP work.

history.details: Inspected three pump guide systems, cleared light rag accumulation at Pump 1, and recorded 121-126 A under matched wet-well conditions. Seal leakage indicators were normal and all VFD fans passed visual inspection.

history.summary: Annual seal and wear clearance service
history.details: Isolated MCC-HW-01, serviced Pump 2 seal chamber, measured impeller wear clearance at 0.82 mm, and replaced contaminated seal oil. Post-service current stabilized at 119-123 A.
Removed woven debris from Pump 3 inlet, inspected the chopper edge, and completed five automatic starts. Wet-well drawdown returned to 48 mm/min with no overload events.

scenario.title: Influent Pump 2 seal leakage and rising VFD current
scenario.description: Investigate Pump 2 seal leakage, rag accumulation, and a 9 percent rise in VFD current before wet-weather standby capacity is reduced.
scenario.fault_summary: Influent pump seal leakage with ragging and rising VFD current
scenario.symptom: Seal moisture alarm and 139 A running current on Pump 2
scenario.production_impact: Loss of Pump 2 reduces wet-weather influent capacity and removes duty/assist redundancy.

lockout_points.isolation_device: MCC-HW-01 Pump 2 feeder and local disconnect
lockout_points.note: Verify zero voltage and prevent automatic wet-well start.

findings.observation: Pump 2 running current reached 139 A against a 124-128 A matched-condition baseline.
Seal moisture alarm annunciated at the station HMI and reset twice on the night shift.
Rag accumulation visible at the Pump 2 guide rail on wet-well camera review.

approved_scope.verified_cause: Mechanical seal wear with ragging load on Pump 2.
lines: Isolate MCC-HW-01 Pump 2 feeder and prove zero energy
Lift Pump 2 and clear rag accumulation from the guide rail
Replace the mechanical seal and wear ring
Reinstall, refill and run a matched-condition current check

history.details: Measured inlet differential pressure at 0.7 kPa, vacuumed the intake plenum, and verified discharge temperature at 78 C under 72 percent load. No surge events were recorded.
Isolated MCC-AER-02, inspected coupling alignment, torqued foundation fasteners, and recorded 2.2 mm/s RMS vibration. The coupling element showed no cracking.
Replaced a fouled inlet filter after differential pressure reached 1.9 kPa. Airflow increased from 8,420 to 9,180 scfm and discharge temperature dropped 6 C.

scenario.title: Blower 2 low airflow and motor thermal trips
scenario.description: Restore basin airflow after repeated motor thermal trips, rising inlet restriction, and coupling-side vibration.
scenario.fault_summary: Turbo blower motor thermal trips with low airflow and coupling vibration
scenario.symptom: Two thermal trips in 48 hours and airflow 11 percent below setpoint
scenario.production_impact: Reduced aeration threatens dissolved-oxygen control in basins 3 and 4 and increases energy consumption.

lockout_points.note: Allow 15 minute spin-down and verify DC bus discharge.

findings.observation: Blower 2 tripped on motor thermal twice within 48 hours.
Basin airflow is running 11 percent below setpoint at the same blower command.
Coupling-side vibration is elevated against the 2.2 mm/s RMS recorded at the last annual service.

approved_scope.verified_cause: Inlet restriction from a loaded filter, with a degraded coupling element adding vibration.
lines: Isolate the MCC-AER-02 blower feeder and prove zero energy
Replace the inlet filter and clean the intake plenum
Replace the coupling element and recheck alignment
Restart and confirm airflow and discharge temperature at setpoint

history.details: Completed clean-water transfer comparison on the basin grid. Standard oxygen transfer efficiency was 5.8 percent below baseline, with the northeast quadrant showing the largest pressure loss.
Mapped pressure at six header taps and confirmed a 4.2 kPa spread across the grid. Air distribution valves were balanced and basin DO response improved by 0.3 mg/L.

affected_component.name: Basin 3 air header and balance valves

history.details: Isolated the west air header and chemically cleaned 96 diffuser discs. Header pressure decreased 3.6 kPa and no membrane tears were observed during restart.

scenario.title: Basin 3 diffuser fouling and uneven DO response
scenario.description: Inspect and replace the failed diffuser sector after rising blower pressure and a persistent low-DO zone near the northeast header.
scenario.fault_summary: Aeration basin diffuser fouling with uneven dissolved oxygen response
scenario.symptom: Header pressure up 5.1 kPa and northeast DO 0.7 mg/L below basin average
scenario.production_impact: Poor oxygen transfer increases blower energy and risks incomplete treatment during peak loading.

findings.observation: Air header pressure has risen 5.1 kPa above the post-cleaning baseline.
Northeast dissolved oxygen reads 0.7 mg/L below the basin average at the same air flow.
The annual transfer test already showed the northeast quadrant with the largest pressure loss.

history.details: Cleaned the channel approach, inspected rake teeth and chain guides, and measured chain sag at 18 mm. Motor current remained 6.1-6.8 A through three loaded cycles.
Locked the channel gate, adjusted both chain take-ups, lubricated guide rollers, and tested the torque limiter at the approved setting. Chain tracking was centered after ten cycles.

history.summary: Cleared screen jam and replaced damaged link
history.details: Removed a timber obstruction, replaced one distorted chain link, and inspected the torque limiter for slip damage. The screen completed 25 automatic cycles without alarm.

scenario.title: Screen 1 chain damage and repeated torque trips
scenario.description: Replace damaged rake-chain links and verify the torque limiter after repeated overload trips under normal debris loading.
scenario.fault_summary: Bar screen motor torque trips with damaged chain links
scenario.symptom: Three overload trips per shift and visible elongation at rake positions 17-20
scenario.production_impact: A screen outage reduces headworks redundancy and increases downstream rag loading.

lockout_points.note: Lock channel gate and verify rake cannot coast or back-drive.

affected_component.name: Screen 1 rake chain and torque limiter

findings.observation: The screen drive is recording three overload trips per shift under normal debris loading.
Visible link elongation at rake positions 17-20.
Operators report the torque limiter resetting without an obstruction being found.

approved_scope.verified_cause: Elongated rake-chain links loading the drive, with a torque limiter that no longer holds its setting.
lines: Lock the channel gate and isolate the MCC-HW-03 screen drive feeder
Replace the damaged chain links at rake positions 17-20
Replace the torque limiter and set it to the approved value
Run 25 automatic cycles and confirm no overload trips

history.details: Recorded 3.1 mm/s RMS at the main bearing and 2.4 mm/s at the gearbox. Differential speed and bowl current remained within the approved operating envelope.
Opened the bowl, measured scroll-flight wear at eight points, replaced two sacrificial tiles, and balanced the rotating assembly. Post-service vibration was 2.5 mm/s RMS.
Replaced a worn progressive-cavity pump stator, recalibrated feed rate, and stabilized cake solids at 22.8 percent. No bowl imbalance alarms occurred after restart.

scenario.title: Centrifuge 2 main-bearing vibration and scroll wear
scenario.description: Inspect the centrifuge after the main-bearing trend crossed alarm and scroll wear accelerated at the solids discharge end.
scenario.fault_summary: Centrifuge main bearing vibration with scroll wear and rotating shaft risk
scenario.symptom: Main bearing vibration 7.2 mm/s RMS and rising bowl temperature
scenario.production_impact: Loss of Centrifuge 2 constrains sludge throughput and increases hauling volume.

findings.observation: Main bearing vibration reached 7.2 mm/s RMS against 3.1 mm/s at the last survey.
Bowl temperature is trending up at unchanged feed rate.
Scroll wear at the solids discharge end has accelerated since the annual inspection.

history.details: Reviewed drive torque trend, inspected the skimmer and center well, and confirmed peak torque at 41 percent during sludge withdrawal. No structural interference was observed.
Collected an oil sample, replaced the breather, topped the gearbox to level, and inspected drive alignment. Particle count remained below the alert threshold.
Removed a lodged timber fragment from the scraper path and verified the overload switch. Running torque returned from 83 percent to 39 percent over one full revolution.

affected_component.name: Clarifier 4 scraper path and overload switch

scenario.title: Clarifier 4 recurring torque overload
scenario.description: Determine whether recurring torque trips originate from a mechanical obstruction, a drifting torque switch, or gearbox deterioration.
scenario.fault_summary: Clarifier gearbox torque overload with possible mechanical obstruction
scenario.symptom: Torque reaches 88 percent near the north quadrant with intermittent false reset
scenario.production_impact: An extended clarifier outage reduces secondary-settling capacity and may force flow restriction.

findings.observation: Drive torque reaches 88 percent near the north quadrant, against a 41 percent monthly peak.
The overload resets intermittently without an operator clearing an obstruction.
A previous torque alarm on this unit was a lodged timber fragment, so an obstruction is not yet ruled out.

history.details: Compared bank intensity sensors, inspected module connectors, and cleaned two reference sleeves. Corrected intensity averaged 91 percent at design flow.
Replaced the scheduled lamp set, cleaned quartz sleeves, inspected wiper seals, and reset lamp-hour counters. All six banks passed intensity verification.

affected_component.name: UV Channel 1 lamp set and quartz sleeves

history.details: Isolated Bank 4, replaced a variable-output ballast, inspected lamp leads, and completed a loaded restart. Bank intensity returned from 72 to 94 percent.

scenario.title: UV Channel 1 low intensity across Bank 2
scenario.description: Restore permit margin after Bank 2 intensity declined with mixed lamp, quartz sleeve, and ballast indications.
scenario.fault_summary: UV lamp intensity loss with ballast voltage alarms and fouled quartz sleeves
scenario.symptom: Bank 2 corrected intensity at 68 percent with two intermittent ballast alarms
scenario.production_impact: Low UV dose creates a discharge-compliance exposure and may require flow restriction.

lockout_points.note: Verify ballast capacitors are discharged and modules are covered before opening.

findings.observation: Bank 2 corrected intensity is 68 percent, against 91 percent measured across banks at the quarterly inspection.
Two intermittent ballast voltage alarms on Bank 2.
Quartz sleeves in Bank 2 show fouling not present at the last lamp replacement.

approved_scope.verified_cause: Combined lamp end-of-life, quartz sleeve fouling and one failing ballast on Bank 2.
lines: Isolate the UV Bank 2 distribution panel and prove zero energy
Replace the Bank 2 lamp set and clean or replace the quartz sleeves
Replace the failing ballast and inspect the lamp leads
Return Bank 2 to service and verify corrected intensity at design flow

history.details: Reviewed normalized permeate flow, salt passage, and stage differential pressure. First-stage differential pressure was 0.4 bar above baseline with stable conductivity.
Completed alkaline and acid CIP sequences, verified heater control, and flushed to conductivity acceptance. Normalized permeate flow recovered 8.7 percent.
Replaced 20 five-micron cartridges after differential pressure reached 1.2 bar. Verified no housing bypass and restored feed pressure to 4.8 bar.

scenario.title: UF/RO Skid 1 permeate decline and high differential pressure
scenario.description: Recover boiler-makeup capacity after membrane scaling, cartridge loading, and an incomplete chemical CIP heat cycle.
scenario.fault_summary: RO membrane scaling with high differential pressure and failed CIP chemical heater
scenario.symptom: Normalized permeate flow down 17 percent and first-stage differential pressure up 1.4 bar
scenario.production_impact: Loss of treated-water output directly limits boiler and process production.

findings.observation: Normalized permeate flow is down 17 percent.
First-stage differential pressure is 1.4 bar above baseline.
The last CIP did not hold its chemical temperature, so the clean was incomplete.

approved_scope.verified_cause: First-stage membrane scaling left in place by a CIP that could not reach chemical temperature.
lines: Replace the CIP chemical heater and verify temperature control
Replace the loaded cartridge filters and check the housings for bypass
Replace the scaled first-stage membrane elements
Run a full CIP and confirm normalized permeate flow and differential pressure

history.details: Recorded motor, gearbox, and fan-bearing vibration on both cells. Cell A gearbox was 2.8 mm/s RMS and oil temperature was 64 C at 83 percent load.

affected_component.name: Cooling Train A fan drives, Cells A and B

history.details: Changed Cell A and B gearbox oil, cleaned magnetic plugs, inspected driveshaft alignment, and verified fan pitch. Oil samples showed no abnormal wear metals.

affected_component.name: Cooling Train A fan gearboxes, Cells A and B

history.details: Isolated Pump A2, replaced the mechanical seal, aligned the coupling, and pressure-tested the casing. Leakage remained zero after a two-hour loaded run.

scenario.title: Cooling Train A fan gearbox vibration
scenario.description: Replace the Cell A fan gearbox and inspect the circulation pump seal after vibration and oil temperature crossed shutdown thresholds.
scenario.fault_summary: Cooling tower fan motor gearbox vibration with rising oil temperature
scenario.symptom: Gearbox vibration 8.1 mm/s RMS and oil temperature 91 C
scenario.production_impact: Loss of one cooling cell reduces heat-rejection margin and can force a production curtailment.

lockout_points.isolation_device: Cooling Tower Cell A fan disconnect
lockout_points.note: Control fan windmilling and verify the driveshaft cannot rotate.

affected_component.name: Cooling Train A Cell A fan gearbox

findings.observation: Cell A gearbox vibration reached 8.1 mm/s RMS, against 2.8 mm/s on the monthly route.
Gearbox oil temperature reached 91 C, against 64 C at 83 percent load.
The annual oil service found no abnormal wear metals, so the change is recent.

history.details: Cleaned the wet well, inspected both guide rails, tested level controls, and recorded Pump 1 drawdown at 37 mm/min. No seal or discharge leakage was observed.

affected_component.name: Lift Station 14 wet well and guide rails

history.summary: Monthly generator exercise and ATS test
history.details: Exercised the generator under station load, verified ATS transfer in 8.4 seconds, checked battery conductance, and confirmed block-heater operation.
Replaced the backup float switch, cleaned the level-transducer stilling tube, and tested alarm callout through the cellular RTU. All alarm states reported correctly.

scenario.title: Lift Station 14 false high-level alarm and Pump 2 current rise
scenario.description: Resolve conflicting level signals and inspect Pump 2 before a remote alarm becomes a wet-well overflow or first-visit failure.
scenario.fault_summary: Wet well false high-level alarm with grinder pump motor current rise
scenario.symptom: Level transducer jumps 0.8 m while float remains normal; Pump 2 current is 14 percent high
scenario.production_impact: A failed remote lift station can overflow the wet well and requires a 22-minute emergency dispatch.

lockout_points.isolation_device: Lift Station 14 pump MCC and generator ATS
lockout_points.note: Disable remote auto-start and isolate normal and standby sources.

affected_component.name: Lift Station 14 level instruments and Pump 2

findings.observation: The level transducer jumps 0.8 m while the float switch stays in its normal state.
Pump 2 running current is 14 percent above its matched-condition baseline.
The high-level callout has been received with no corresponding wet-well condition on arrival.

procurement_children.title: Expedite centrifuge main bearing
procurement_children.description: Confirm OEM interchangeability, lead time, freight, and arrival inspection for the Centrifuge 2 main bearing.

procurement_children.title: Source clarifier drive gearbox
procurement_children.description: Validate the gearbox ratio, output flange, torque rating, and delivery commitment before approving Clarifier 4 replacement.

procurement_children.title: Expedite cooling tower fan gearbox
procurement_children.description: Confirm fan gearbox shaft orientation, service factor, oil package, and crane delivery window for Cooling Train A.

procurement_children.title: Confirm grinder pump emergency spare
procurement_children.description: Verify the NP 3202 grinder configuration, guide-rail fit, cable length, and emergency delivery route for Lift Station 14.
